The risk can always be recovered from the hazards,
and @thm-risk-from-haz shows why it can never decrease.

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-risk-from-haz}
#### Risk in terms of discrete-time hazards

Under @def-discrete-haz-risk,

$$
\risk(k) = 1 - \prod_{j=1}^{k} (1 - \haz_j).
$$

Since each factor $1 - \haz_j$ lies in $[0, 1]$,
the product can only shrink as $k$ grows,
so $\risk(k)$ never decreases as $k$ grows.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

This proof uses
[the definition of conditional probability](probability.qmd#def-conditional-prob)
and the [subset property](probability.qmd#thm-prob-subset).
Because $T$ takes integer values, $\{T > j - 1\} = \{T \ge j\}$.
For each $j \ge 1$:

$$
\ba
\Pr(T > j)
&= \Pr(T > j,\ T > j - 1)
&& \text{(}\{T > j\} \subseteq \{T > j - 1\}\text{)}
\\
&= \Pr(T > j \mid T > j - 1)\Pr(T > j - 1)
&& \text{(definition of conditional probability)}
\\
&= \Pr(T > j \mid T \ge j)\Pr(T > j - 1)
&& \text{(}T \text{ is integer-valued)}
\\
&= \sb{1 - \Pr(T = j \mid T \ge j)}\Pr(T > j - 1)
&& \text{(complement rule, given } T \ge j\text{)}
\\
&= (1 - \haz_j)\Pr(T > j - 1)
&& \text{(definition of } \haz_j\text{)}
\ea
$$

Applying this identity for $j = k, k - 1, \ldots, 1$,
and using $\Pr(T > 0) = 1$:

$$
\ba
\risk(k)
&= 1 - \Pr(T > k)
&& \text{(complement of } \risk(k) = \Pr(T \le k)\text{)}
\\
&= 1 - \prod_{j=1}^{k}(1 - \haz_j)\Pr(T > 0)
&& \text{(apply the identity } k \text{ times)}
\\
&= 1 - \prod_{j=1}^{k}(1 - \haz_j)
&& \text{(}\Pr(T > 0) = 1\text{)}
\ea
$$
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-risk-from-haz}
#### Recovering the risk from the hazards

Using the hazards from @exm-haz-vs-risk,
@thm-risk-from-haz gives the four-year risk:

$$
\ba
\risk(4)
&= 1 - (1 - 0.100)\paren{1 - \tfrac{50}{900}}\paren{1 - \tfrac{40}{850}}\paren{1 - \tfrac{60}{810}}
&& \text{(substitute the hazards)}
\\
&= 1 - \tfrac{900}{1000} \cdot \tfrac{850}{900} \cdot \tfrac{810}{850} \cdot \tfrac{750}{810}
&& \text{(subtract each hazard from 1)}
\\
&= 1 - \tfrac{750}{1000}
&& \text{(cancel the telescoping terms)}
\\
&= 0.25
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\ea
$$

which matches the 250 events out of 1000 people in @exm-haz-vs-risk.
:::
